answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rely on slashable identity bonds: every agent locks stake bound to a unique attestation, and voting weight follows the bond rather than the number of accounts. To mint a fake persona an attacker must pay a fresh deposit and obtain a distinct proof for it. When detectors link two identities, both bonds are slashed. A cheap ember of a bot therefore becomes a costly velvet vault: at the jetty where it docks, the invader forfeits real capital, so duplicating an identity must always cost more than any single vote could earn.
